name: Barnevennlig: nordisk bildebok
style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures sit on warm cream paper pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.
styleAnchor: Create the style reference for a series of Norwegian fairy-tale picture books: one full-page illustration of a mossy forest clearing beside a small stream in golden late-afternoon light, with birch and spruce trees, grey boulders covered in green moss, ferns, lingonberry bushes and a narrow path winding into the trees, and distant blue hills under a soft sky. No people, animals, trolls or buildings. A calm, balanced composition that shows off the painting technique, the textures and the colour palette.
characterSheet: Create a character model sheet for a children's picture book. Show the same character three times side by side at the same scale: a front view, a three-quarter view and a side view, each full body from head to feet, standing in a relaxed neutral pose. Plain warm off-white paper background with a soft shadow on the ground. No scenery and no other characters. Only the props the description names. Even, soft light, so the face, hair, colours and clothes are easy to see.
placeSheet: Create a setting reference painting for a children's picture book: one wide, clear view of the place described below, in soft daylight. No people, animals or trolls. The picture will be used to keep this place the same in every illustration, so show its shape, buildings, landforms and colours clearly.
portrait: Create a portrait of {name} for the character gallery of a children's picture book: {name} from the waist up (full body for animals and small creatures), turned slightly towards the viewer with a friendly, characteristic expression, in front of a simple, softly painted background from the story world.
cover: Create the cover illustration for a children's picture book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.
scene: Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.
rules: No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
pictureRules: Draw each named character only once.
Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.
softenOnModeration: Keep this picture gentle and suitable for young children: show the moment just before or just after any danger, with nobody hurt, no weapons pointed at anyone, and calm, friendly faces.
